title: Pylon vs Salesforce Service Cloud for B2B support | Pylon
summary: Compare Pylon and Salesforce Service Cloud on channels, agents, CRM sync, and pricing. Keep Salesforce as CRM, or stay on Service Cloud.
body_markdown:
Choose Pylon when B2B customers reach you in Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, and chat, and your team needs agents that investigate with account, product, and support context already loaded. Choose Salesforce Service Cloud when support should stay on Salesforce CRM records, entitlements, and contact-center workflows your org already runs.


You can keep Salesforce as the CRM and move support work to Pylon. That split is the decision this post is for. For a wider shortlist of other platforms, see[7 Salesforce Service Cloud alternatives for B2B support](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/salesforce-service-cloud-alternatives) .


Disclosure: this post is published by Pylon. We stick to what each vendor says on its own public pages, checked Nov 9, 2026.

## What is the difference between Pylon and Salesforce Service Cloud?


Salesforce Service Cloud is Salesforce’s service product: cases, routing, knowledge, entitlements, and Agentforce, built for teams that want support on the same CRM the rest of the company uses. It fits companies already deep in Salesforce. Service Cloud includes Flex Credits per org on Core (500K), Advanced (1M), and Max (2.75M per year); an AI agent is included in Advanced, and Max adds the full Agentforce for Service suite.


Pylon is the agentic support platform purpose-built for B2B. It is the help desk itself (ticketing, SLAs, knowledge base, channels, and agents), not an AI layer you attach to Service Cloud. Agents use Support, Account, and Product Intelligence to investigate and act while people direct and review the work. Pylon is trusted by 1,800+ B2B customers.


## Can you keep Salesforce CRM and replace Service Cloud?


Yes. Pylon’s Salesforce integration documents account matching, field sync in either direction, contact sync, account details beside issues, and daily AI conversation-summary activity sync to the Salesforce Account. That is a concrete way to keep commercial data in Salesforce while moving support queues, channels, and agent workflows to Pylon.


Define the boundary before you migrate:


- Which platform owns accounts, contacts, commercial fields, and support commitments?
- Which fields sync, in which direction, and how conflicts resolve?
- Where do people find the authoritative support history?
- Which automations need a service event, a CRM update, or a human approval?


Pylon’s sync does not mean every custom object, Flow, entitlement, report, or historical record transfers automatically. Test the workflows that matter with a sample first.


## How do Pylon agents compare with Agentforce?


Both platforms offer customer-facing resolution and assistance for teammates. The operating model is where they diverge.


On Pylon, Assist Agent investigates and acts for teammates, Support Agent works customer questions, Slack Agent answers and acts from Slack, and Automations start repeatable work from events or schedules. Skills are reusable instructions people and agents share. With Automations set to start on new issues, agents investigate issues before your team opens them.[Nexus](https://www.usepylon.com/nexus) describes the context, permissions, approvals, and traces behind that work.


On Salesforce, Agentforce for Service runs on Salesforce data, knowledge, workflows, and the actions your team configures. That can include external systems through Salesforce’s own integration stack. The buying decision is whether your team wants agents inside a B2B help desk with standing account and product context, or agents inside the Salesforce service configuration you already maintain.


For more on agent types and platforms, see[AI agents in customer support](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/ai-agents-customer-support) ,[Types of AI support agents](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/types-of-ai-support-agents) , and[A guide to agentic AI platforms](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/agentic-ai-platform) .


## How does pricing compare?


Pylon is seats plus agentic credits. Professional is $89 per seat per month and Advanced is $139 per seat per month on an annual contract. Enterprise is a custom quote. Agentic features (Assist Agent, Support Agent, Slack Agent, Automations, AI issue QA, backtesting) run on credits. The minimum credit commitment is 5,000 credits. Pylon does not charge per issue. Skills are included and do not use credits. See[How agentic support is priced](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/how-agentic-support-is-priced) .


Salesforce Service Cloud is priced per user by edition. The public comparison table lists Core at $195, Advanced at $395, and Max at $550 per user/month on annual contracts. AI usage draws from Flex Credit pools by edition, with Agentforce packaging that depends on Core, Advanced, or Max. We do not publish specific Flex Credit unit rates here. Quote Salesforce’s current Agentforce page when you model a deal.


A fair comparison uses your renewal proposal on one side and a Pylon quote sized to seats, credits, channels, and Salesforce sync on the other. Include implementation, admin time, and AI consumption at 1× and 2× volume.


## When should you stay on Service Cloud?


Stay when support depends on Salesforce’s service data model, entitlements, industry products, or contact-center configuration, and your team has the admin capacity to keep that system current. Moving software is not an improvement if it recreates the same dependencies elsewhere.


Salesforce’s pricing page lists case management, service contracts and entitlements, routing, Slack collaboration, AI, and contact-center options. It is fair to treat Service Cloud as a full service platform for orgs standardized on Salesforce. The question is whether that configured system serves your B2B support workflow better than a dedicated help desk after total cost and change risk.


## When should you evaluate Pylon?


Evaluate Pylon when customers expect Slack Connect or Microsoft Teams as a support channel, investigations need account and product context beyond the CRM case, or support wants to change workflows without a Salesforce development cycle.


Findigs moved from Service Cloud to Pylon. Tatiana Meduna, Head of Business Operations at Findigs, said: "Maintaining our growth trajectory on Service Cloud would have required doubling our support team. In the age of AI and automation, that doesn't make sense." Full story:[How Findigs replaced Salesforce Service Cloud](https://www.usepylon.com/case-study/findigs) . After the move, Findigs cut ticket volume 30%, automatically triaged 15% of tickets through AI runbooks, and avoided 2x headcount growth.


Across 300+ migrations from Zendesk, Intercom, and Salesforce, 90% finished in under 2 months. The[Salesforce Service migration guide](https://support.usepylon.com/articles/2789482238-migrating-from-salesforce-service) covers contacts, accounts, cases, custom fields, and knowledge base content. Migrated cases arrive closed. Timing still depends on your channels, history, and Salesforce field map. Validate a sample before cutover.


Pylon is the help desk, not an Agentforce add-on. If you only want an agent on top of Service Cloud, Pylon is not that product.


## FAQ


### What is the difference between Pylon and Salesforce Service Cloud?


Salesforce Service Cloud is Salesforce’s service product for teams that want cases and Agentforce on Salesforce CRM records. Pylon is the agentic support platform purpose-built for B2B: the full help desk with agents, channels, and account context. See also[Pylon vs Salesforce](https://www.usepylon.com/competitors/salesforce) .


### Can we keep Salesforce CRM and move support to Pylon?


Yes. Pylon documents Salesforce account matching, field sync in either direction, contact sync, account details on the issue, and daily conversation-summary activity sync. Define ownership and test the workflows you need before cutover.


### How much does each platform cost?


Pylon Professional is $89 per seat per month and Advanced is $139 per seat per month on an annual contract. Enterprise is custom. Agentic features run on credits (minimum 5,000). Salesforce Service Cloud lists Core at $195, Advanced at $395, and Max at $550 per user/month on its comparison table, with Flex Credits by edition for Agentforce. Model both with your real seat count and AI usage.


### Is Pylon an AI add-on for Service Cloud?


No. Pylon is the help desk. Salesforce can remain connected as the CRM while support runs in Pylon.


### How long does a Service Cloud migration take?


It depends on channels, integrations, historical data, and the Salesforce fields you need. Across 300+ migrations from Zendesk, Intercom, and Salesforce, 90% finished in under 2 months. Validate a sample import before setting cutover dates.


### Which should B2B support teams pick?


Our editorial pick for account-aware support in Slack, Teams, email, and chat is Pylon. Service Cloud remains the stronger fit when your org is standardized on Salesforce service operations and contact-center products.
